What makes cheetahs so amazing?

The fastest animal on Earth, the cheetah is a hunter that runs like the wind. The moment it takes off, it reaches an incredible speed in an instant.

We've gathered all sorts of stories about cheetahs here — cheetah facts, cheetah speed, cheetah ecology, and more.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about cheetahs

A cheetah's top speed is over 110 km/h, and it reaches 100 km/h just 3 seconds after taking off. But it can only sprint at full speed for 20-30 seconds, about 300 m. Its long tail acts as a counterbalance when it changes direction, and its claws grip the ground firmly. Its hunting success rate is about 58%, and it can't roar — it communicates with purrs and chirps instead. It's a vulnerable species, with fewer than 7,100 left in the wild.

Great points to observe together

Point out things like the high speed (110 km/h), the short sprint (300 m), the long tail (balance), and not being able to roar. It's fun to talk together about "Why can't a cheetah run for long?"

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Run in place as fast as you can for 3 seconds and experience "fast like a cheetah — but only for a moment!" Comparing its markings and speed with a leopard's (spots vs. rosettes) makes it even more interesting.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How fast is a cheetah?
A. Over 110 km/h, reaching 100 km/h just 3 seconds after taking off. But it can only run about 300 m.

Q. Can a cheetah roar?
A. No. It can't roar — it communicates with purrs and chirps, like a cat.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Trying a 3-second sprint and comparing its markings and speed with a leopard's both work well.
